Epistory has a lot of charm, however there is a strange difficulty curve between the relaxing exploration/puzzle solving with enemies sprinkled around and the swarm challenges, especially in early game areas. Some of these challenges felt so long with no half-way respawn point, really dreaded having to redo any of them if i failed. Additionally, the light colored text blends with the watercolor/pastel color palette in some areas, adding to the already hectic challenge. Allowing players to adjust enemy speed or have an invincible practice mode might've helped. Despite that, i did finish the story as it was an enjoyable enough game I didn't completely abandon it. I have no desire to do all the achievements or find all the fragments but it was a nice time. Flame was my MVP element. 

Understandably, I think a skilled typist or someone who doesn't enjoy slow paced puzzles might find this game boring. Even as a puzzle enthusiast, some puzzles were pretty annoying. I didn't enjoy the ice area at all, but you can get through most puzzles with some persistence and patience. A lot of areas have mazes, which some might find tedious. A less skilled typist might rage quite, but it could be a good way to test skills. It's a unique experience and overall a decent game worth checking out if you enjoy typing and puzzles, while forgiving some issues.

The actual gameplay of this is miserable. This is the first typing game I've ever played and it genuinely made me reconsider ever purchasing another.

Walking in this game is so clunky and not good, and you can really tell when you start getting to all the sliding ice stuff. I don't hate sliding ice puzzles but I do if the movement is already bad.

There's some kind of annoying QoL things, like sometimes you knockback enemies just barely off the screen so it removes the word and when it is visible again you have to restart. I think making sprinting and quick travel perks I have to purchase is not great. The map could be better since it only has 'whole map' and 'zoomed in where you're standing' options. There's an ability to let you see objectives which is pretty bad since you have to stop to even use it (and it disappears once you start walking) and you also can't control what objective it directs you to (also doesn't work in dungeons). The fire burn magic also is kind of wonky since I kept running into the issue of still having to type the word because the burn takes too long and you can't start on the word underneath until the word is totally gone.

My biggest complaint though, and what made me throw in my towel, is how bad the typing battle waves are.

When I have ten things on my screen moving at different speeds, I need to very clearly be able to see what word I am on. SO MANY TIMES I would try to type a word of a bug about to be up on me but somewhere on the screen there was a word I hadn't finished or the game thought I wanted to type a different word with the same starting letter.

It only gets worse when you start adding in the elemental stuff, which is what ended up being the nail for me for the second wave. I got through almost the whole wave, no issues, right up until I needed to switch elements back and forth, and I had the 'why isn't the letter c working what bug on my screen could have possibly started with an i' crap happen. I still don't know what word it thought I was on or what it wanted me to type because you also lose instantly when a bug reaches you and you have to start the wave over.

It's frustrating. It's not fun. I should be losing because I'm slow at typing, not because I can't figure out what letter I'm supposed to type next. I think if it wasn't for this one specific issue, I would have kept playing at least to finish it.

Just finished this game, and I will say - it's lovely, but it's not without its flaws.
Let's start with what I liked:
1. Typing gameplay!! I've never played a game where typing was a core mechanic, so it was really fun
2. The puzzles were challenging, but it was the right amount of challenging. It took a little circling (literally, in some cases) but I was able to solve them
3. The voice acting is really good! 
4. The art direction is really unique and cool. The origami aesthetic was really sweet

Now for what I didn't quite like:
1. Sometimes, I'd mistype and end up frozen because I'd accidentally hit the first letter of one of the other powers - essentially leaving me open to die when facing barrages of enemies
2. Some of the words were quite difficult and I'd have to slow down. This is personal preference, obviously, and I don't fault the devs for it at all - it did expand my vocabulary :)
3. The art style completely changed for the ending cinematic. I won't say I disliked it, it was more so jarring to see.

Overall - I think it's a gorgeous game and it's got me interested in finding more games like this!

Epistory is a game that successfully combines an action adventure game with RPG elements and typing! Words appear over enemies and you must type the words as fast as you can to kill the enemies before they reach you. You are also given magical abilities; lightning, fire, ice and wind each with its own unique properties, i.e fire destroys the next word, ice freezes enemies, wind pushes enemies back and lighting can destroy words on other enemies.

+ Killing enemies rewards you with experience allowing you to upgrade different magical abilities and attributes.
+ Amazing narrative that kind of hides in the background, revealed towards the end
+ Unique Art style

Conclusion:
The entire game is controlled by keyboard, I highly doubt steam controller will be viable for this game. This is a fun casual game that was a huge surprise for me. For those looking for a fun game and want to improve your typing speed, this is a great game.

높은 등급의 벌레나 오브젝트의 경우에는 2개 이상의 입력을 요구하기도 하기에 다수의 적이 등장할때에는 가까운 적을 우선하여 빠르게 타이핑을 하여야 합니다.
만약, 제때에 벌레들을 처치하지 못하고 닿게 되면... 그대로 게임오버가 되어 이전 시점부터 다시 진행해야 하죠.

몬스터들은 중 일부는 속성이 존재하며, 이를 텍스트의 색상으로 구분할 수 있습니다.
일반적으로는 하얀색으로 등장하여 속성에 상관없이 제거할 수 있고, 붉은색은 불 속성으로, 푸른색은 얼음 속성으로 제거할 수 있죠.
총 4개의 속성이 존재하며 속성에 따라서 추가적인 효과가 발생하기도 합니다.
붉은색은 불을 일으켜서 다음 순서의 텍스트를 제거해주는 효과가 있고, 얼음은 상대를 일정시간 얼려버릴 수 있죠.
전기는 몬스터가 생존한 경우 인접한 다른 몬스터에게 전격을 전이시켜 연속 피해를 입힐 수 있고, 바람은 경로상의 적들을 후방으로 밀어낼 수 있습니다.

속성은 몬스터들의 처치나 특수 효과 외에도 맵의 다양한 오브젝트들과의 상호작용에도 사용됩니다.
길을 막는 가시덤불을 불을 이용하여 제거할 수 있고, 강을 얼려서 얼음 빙판 길을 만들어낼 수도 있죠.
전기를 공급하여 기계장치를 작동시킨다거나 바람을 일으켜 숨겨진 공간 또는 순간이동 장치를 활성화할 수도 있습니다.
이들을 활용하는 약간의 퍼즐적인 공간들도 등장하여 타이핑 실력 외의 머리 쓰는 능력도 요구하죠.

이렇게 몬스터들을 처치하고 여기저기 있는 오브젝트와 상자를 오픈하면서 깃펜같은 포인트를 얻을 수 있습니다.
이를 모아 콤보 시간 증가라거나 각 속성 효과의 강화, 이동속도 증가 등 다양한 스킬들을 강화할 수 있는 포인트를 얻을 수 있죠.
또한, 상자 중 던전에서 등장하는 일부에서는 사진 조각을 획득하여 스토리와 관련된 갤러리를 획득하여 감상을 할 수 있습니다.

특정 포인트를 누적하게 되면 지역 확장이 가능하다는 안내가 등장합니다.
지도를 확인하여 확장 마크가 있는 곳으로 향하면 활성화할 수 있으며, 이를 통해 모험을 할 수 있는 영역이 확장되죠.
숨겨진 길들과 상자들이 등장하고 숨겨진 스토리 또는 속성을 얻을 수 있는 메인 스토리 던전들도 등장하여 도전할 수 있습니다.
일부 지역들은 특정 속성을 활용하여 길을 만들어내거나 장치들을 작동시킬 수 있기에 마구잡이 확장보다는 순서대로 진행하는게 필요하기도 하죠.

This is a fun little adventure, but it probably won't make you any better at typing. The concept is inspired, if not an amalgam of disparate concepts, as you are a girl on a fox who is attacking insect nests by spelling words to proceed. The graphics and music are great, but I find the tired "narrator voice telling the story as you play" cliche kind of dull and dragged it down a bit for me, especially since there really isn't any story. Uncovering parts of the map is really well done, and the game gets progressively harder as it goes on, making it a decent enough challenge while still being very easy. 

You basically spell words to manipulate obstacles and defeat enemies. You soon get four elemental abilities that vary the game play, though once you get the lightning the game gets too easy since you can chain attack multiple enemies at once and any challenge the game had ended here. There are simplistic puzzles and the exploration element is overall well done. I like the fact that you can buy upgrades and the game overall had just enough depth to keep me playing through to the end. Unfortunately, some of the achievements are terrible and I had to spend hours grinding in the arena to unlock them. Further, the arena itself is broken since people have cracked the game's code and most of the scores on there are from people using cheats.

The reason it won't make you any better at typing is because you aren't typing logical sentences but rather random words with abrupt stops. I noticed some typing errors that I made without realizing it, but the game didn't really give any guidance on correcting these mistakes. The only thing I really learned was that typing is more of a mental exercise more than anything, at least for someone who types regularly. I would get stumped up on certain words while others I could type immediately. If you're already competent at typing you will breeze through this, and if not, it probably won't make you any better. Also, the "adaptive mode" seems to not do anything other than make the game ridiculously easy if you fail over and over. Presumably, because that never happened while I played, and playing perfect didn't make the game much harder.

Most fun I have had while playing a typing game. I already picked up the sequel to play next. The strategy of switching between the different powers made its combat engaging enough that I struggled to walk away from a bug nest without defeating it. The art style is also superb; everything is made out of paper which fits well with the type of game it is.

On the downside I did not care much about the story. It did not negatively affect my gameplay, bug I mostly ignored it which was fine. The other issue was that it missed some core features that I think would have helped me learn to type more than it did. Namely, a mode to start with less of the keyboard and work up to using more of it, a mode to add numbers/symbols to the regular mix, and tracking which keys I regularly mess up and having me use those keys more until I always get them right.

Over all still worth buying and I plan to use the arena mode to continue improve typing & get the last few achievements, but I hope the second one has a few more features to help me learn to type better.
